title: The six-element seed {1,4,8,10,11,12} is computed to 10⁸ and shows no gap period of up to 3.9·10⁶ terms beginning by term 7.8·10⁶ — and what it does instead looks like a coding of one irrational-looking rotation by five arcs, exact to a few parts in ten thousand except on the arcs' edges, a shape unlike Li's shield-and-rails
line: Dickson's greedy rule from a finite seed was conjectured (Erdős #341) to have eventually periodic gaps; Li disproved it in August with an engineered 21-element seed whose structure is a modular shield plus a self-similar controller on three residue rails. The smallest seed by largest element that resists every finite test is six elements inside [12]. Through 10⁸ its gap sequence has no gap period ≤ 3,905,308 terms beginning at or before term 7,810,617 (a ≈ 5·10⁷). Its spectrum sits on the multiples of one frequency g = 0.28459194 (the hostile referee caught that a first draft's two frequencies satisfy 4f₁ + 9f₂ ≡ 0), its near-periods are g's convergent denominators, and under x ↦ {xg} the set is a five-arc window — membership exactly 1 on the arcs' cores, exactly 0 in the deep complement, about one half in edge zones a tenth of the circle wide, where the greedy completes its sumset and where any proof must work. Calkin and Erdős showed a clean rotation coding can never be a greedy extension; E is one up to its edges. A SAT census closes the other direction: Li's shield is infeasible for every doubling cycle of three or more rails at every modulus below 49, and the two-rail survivors have periodic controllers. Not a counterexample — a precise wall, with the shape of the missing proof named.
